beats.content:
WordPress reads the comment at the top of `style.css` and shows it under **Appearance > Themes**. Here is your theme's header:

```css
/*
Theme Name: My Block Theme
Author: You
Description: My first block theme, built with Learn WordPress, reimagined.
Version: 1.0.0
Requires at least: 6.6
Tested up to: 7.1
Requires PHP: 7.4
License: GNU General Public License v2 or later
License URI: https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-2.0.html
Text Domain: my-block-theme
*/
```

- `Theme Name` is the one that matters most. If it's missing, WordPress falls back to showing the folder name.
- The WordPress.org Theme Directory requires the rest too: `Author`, `Description`, `Version`, `Requires at least`, `Tested up to`, `Requires PHP`, `License`, `License URI` and `Text Domain`.
- `Requires at least: 6.6` is there because theme.json version 3 arrived in WordPress 6.6.

You can still write CSS below the header, but WordPress doesn't load it on its own. A theme that needs it enqueues it from `functions.php`. In a block theme, most styling belongs in theme.json anyway.
beats.question: Which header line would you change first to make this theme yours?

beats.content:
`settings` in theme.json decides what the editor offers. Two useful settings:

- `settings.color.palette` is your list of colours, each with `name`, `slug` and `color`. They appear in every colour picker.
- `settings.color.defaultPalette` set to `false` hides WordPress's own default colours, so people only see yours.

Another is `settings.appearanceTools`. Set it to `true` and WordPress switches on a bundle of design controls in one go, including border, spacing (block gap, margin and padding), line height, and link, heading, button and caption colour controls.

```json
"settings": {
  "appearanceTools": true,
  "color": {
    "defaultPalette": false,
    "palette": [ ... ]
  }
}
```

Settings don't change how anything looks by themselves. They decide which tools and presets are available. Styles (a later lesson) use them.
beats.goal: See how settings shape the editor.

checks.message: theme.json must be valid JSON once your new settings are in. Check commas between entries and keys.
Add a palette entry with the slug accent. Like the others, it needs a name, a slug and a color with a hex value. Keep version 3 in theme.json.
Set the content width. It lives in a layout object inside settings, not at the top level.
Set the wide width next to the content width, inside the same layout object.
